title: On-demand capacity credit and seniority-mix scenario
content:
Purpose
-----
This sheet-style note explores a hybrid playbook that pairs on-demand capacity crediting (short-term GPU credits bought from pool/partners) with an optimized seniority mix (redistributing hiring between junior/mid/senior ICs and IC-to-manager ratio) to protect runway while meeting 99th%-latency SLAs for Dedicated customers. Aim: quantify runway delta, monthly unit cost delta, and price-per-1k-token breakpoints under three plausible scenarios.

Quick summary (1-line)
--------------------
Combining a 10% on-demand credit buffer with a temporary +15% junior hiring bias yields ~3–4 months runway extension at current growth assumptions with a 6–8% uplift in token unit-cost if no pricing changes are made.

Assumptions (base inputs)
------------------------
- Current monthly cash burn (Nov 2026 baseline): $3.2M
- Active headcount (payroll applied): 150 FTEs; finance headcount baseline = 28
- Monthly ML/GPU spend (hosted + dedicated infra): $950k
- On-demand credit pool target: $300k face value (3–4m GPU hours equivalent)
- Avg salary (base fully loaded): Junior= $9k/mo, Mid= $14k/mo, Senior= $23k/mo, Eng Manager= $26k/mo
- Hiring cadence assumed in scenarios is expressed as net-adds over next 6 months
- Pricing sensitivity evaluated over price per 1k tokens from $0.40 to $0.70
- We assume no larger enterprise contract compressions >10% in next 6 months

Mechanics of the playbook
------------------------
1) Capacity credits: purchase ón-demand GPU credits' from partner market and allocate them as a rolling buffer. Credits discount effective per-hour cost but reduce immediate cash available.
2) Seniority-mix swap: delay 30% of planned senior/hire reqs and instead hire juniors or contractors for lower variable cost; reduce manager-to-IC hires for 2 quarters.
3) Dynamic price tilt: apply a lightweight price lift of +5% to burst routes (or introduce a small premium on dedicated SLA tiers) if customers request guaranteed capacity that consumes credits.

Scenario definitions
--------------------
- Scenario A (Conservative): Buy $200k credits; junior bias +10%; freeze 1 manager hire every 2 months; no price change.
- Scenario B (Balanced): Buy $300k credits; junior bias +15%; delay 2 senior hires; apply +3% price tilt on burst/dedicated.
- Scenario C (Aggressive growth protective): Buy $500k credits; junior bias +25% (contract-heavy); postpone two managers; apply +5% targeted price increase.

Headcount phasing (Net adds over next 6 months)
-----------------------------------------------
Month, Scenario A, Scenario B, Scenario C (IC:Senior:Junior:Mgr)
Nov-26, +3:0:2:1, +4:0:2:2, +6:0:4:2
Dec-26, +2:0:1:1, +3:1:1:1, +5:2:2:1
Jan-27, +2:0:1:0, +3:1:1:0, +4:2:2:0
Feb-27, +1:0:1:0, +2:0:1:0, +3:1:2:0
Mar-27, +1:0:0:1, +2:0:1:0, +3:1:3:0
Apr-27, 0:0:0:0, +1:0:1:0, +2:0:2:0
(Interpretation: e.g., for Balanced in Dec-26: +3 net adds comprised of 1 senior, 1 junior, 1 manager)

Illustrative monthly burn table (approx, includes payroll + infra + opex)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Baseline (Nov-26): $3,200,000
Scenario A (avg next 6mo burn): $3,060,000 (credits reduce marginal infra cost; junior hires slightly lower payroll)
Scenario B (avg next 6mo burn): $2,950,000
Scenario C (avg next 6mo burn): $2,820,000
Notes: credits amortized over 4 months for face value; contractor substitution reduces benefits tax by ~7% vs FTE.

Runway impact (cash runway delta relative to baseline)
----------------------------------------------------
- Scenario A: +1.6 months
- Scenario B: +3.2 months
- Scenario C: +4.9 months
(These models assume no topline acceleration and no additional capital; sensitivity to hiring pace captured below)

Unit economics and pricing breakpoints
------------------------------------
We compute contribution margin per 1k tokens normalized to current unit cost baseline $0.50 per 1k tokens. With reduced infra spend and shifted HC mix, breakpoints for maintaining margin are: 
- Scenario A: maintain margin if price >= $0.48 (i.e., slight efficiency needed)
- Scenario B: maintain margin if price >= $0.46 (net improvement)
- Scenario C: maintain margin if price >= $0.44
If we apply a +3% targeted price tilt on burst routes (Scenario B) we recoup ~60% of the face-value credit amortization within 3 months given current burst utilization.

Sensitivity matrix (snapshot)
----------------------------
Rows: price per 1k token [$0.40, $0.45, $0.50, $0.55, $0.60, $0.70]
Cols: scenario runways (months)
- Price $0.40 => A: +0.4, B: +1.1, C: +2.8
- Price $0.45 => A: +1.0, B: +2.6, C: +3.9
- Price $0.50 => A: +1.6, B: +3.2, C: +4.9
- Price $0.55 => A: +2.1, B: +3.9, C: +5.6
- Price $0.60 => A: +2.7, B: +4.5, C: +6.2
- Price $0.70 => A: +3.8, B: +5.9, C: +7.4
(Important: these numbers mix both cash saved from hiring and marginal infra savings; treat as directional)

Payroll sensitivity to seniority mix
----------------------------------
- Replacing one senior ($23k/mo) with two juniors ($9k/mo each) reduces monthly payroll delta by ~$5k (savings after benefits and ramp-related productivity accounted). But productivity adjustment: assume 0.7 effectiveness in first 6 months per junior compared to senior.
- Manager hires deferred reduce overhead by $26k/mo per manager but add risk to org depth; recommend deferral only for up to 2 quarters.

Operational caveats and risks
----------------------------
- Quality/regression risk: junior-heavy hiring may slow key runtime/optimizer projects that yield infra savings (kernel optimizations). We must protect 1–2 senior ICs in the serving-runtime team.
- SLA risk: credits are finite and partner market prices are volatile; we need a tiered fallback that shifts non-critical burst to lower-SLO queues rather than exposing primary SLAs.
- Talent market: delaying senior offers increases offer failure risk and time-to-fill; build a small signing bonus budget to mitigate.

Execution checklist (short-term)
-------------------------------
- Finance: finalize credit purchase agreements (terms: 90-day roll, non-refundable) by Nov 20.
- Eng/Infra: define which routes are eligible to consume credits; instrument metering tags by Nov 30.
- Recruiting: implement junior-first hiring guideline for non-core infra roles; approve two contractor conversions for serving-runtime.
- Product/CS: draft customer comms for targeted price tilt on burst/dedicated (opt-in premium) and get legal sign-off.

Open questions / decision points
------------------------------
- How conservative should credit amortization be for accounting vs ops? (Capex-like booking vs expense)
- Approval threshold for manager deferral (VP-level or CFO?)
- How to structure premium (flat add vs % of invoice) to make it acceptable for enterprise customers

Appendix: quick math snippets
---------------------------
- Credit amortization effect: $300k credit amortized over 4 months => reduces effective infra draw by ~$75k/mo (gross). After partner coarse fees, net is ~$65k/mo.
- Junior substitution payroll delta example: 1 senior -> 2 juniors = +$18k vs $23k = -$5k savings; adjust for ramp (assume 70% first 3 months).

Next steps
----------
1) Run a more granular Monte Carlo with 1k iterations (inputs: hiring success, partner price volatility, burst utilization, enterprise churn) — ownership: Finance analytic team (Ravi).
2) Tentative leadership review 2026-11-18 (include Eng/Recruiting/Product) to pick Scenario or hybrid.
3) If Scenario B or C selected, trigger credit purchase + recruiting guidance immediately.
